THE ELECTRICAL AGE. OCTOBER, 1949
FINNISH REFLECTIONS
By CAROLINE HASLETT
I FLEW into Finland soon after the Armistice in 1945, and was impressed, as I had been before the war, by the austere charm of the country, and now even more by the hospitality and indomitable spirit of the people in the midst of much bleakness. In June, 1949, I flew again to Finland to attend a meeting of the Board of Directors of the International Federation of Business and Professional Women, and could assess in some measure the progress made in face of heavy odds.

In helping to rebuild the country, Finland's women are taking their traditional role of many centuries, for it was on the basis of men and women working together that modern Finnish society was built, and in 1906 Finland was the first country in Europe to grant equal suffrage between men and women. I was honoured to propose a vote of thanks to Miina Sillanpaa, who rose from humble origins to become Finland's first Cabinet Minister, followed later by two other women.
